summary: Summarizes the relationship between the IETF and the Internet Society after the 2018 restructuring into IASA 2.0. The change altered the IETF's administrative, legal, and financial structure, so this document revises RFC 2031.

plainLanguage.summary: The IETF and the Internet Society are partners. When the IETF changed how it is run, this wrote down how the partnership works now.

questions: what does isoc do for the ietf
what is the relationship between ietf and isoc
subtitle: A short summary of how the IETF and the Internet Society work together after the 2018 IASA 2.0 restructuring.

tldr.problem: The 2018 IASA 2.0 restructuring changed the IETF's administrative, legal and financial arrangements, which made the older description of its relationship with ISOC in RFC 2031 out of date.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC restates the relationship at a high level: ISOC has no direct influence on the technical content of standards, plays a small role in the process, and supports the new IETF LLC, its subsidiary, legally and financially.
tldr.outcome: It replaces RFC 2031 as the summary of the IETF-ISOC relationship and sets no new technical or security rules.

today: RFC 8712 replaces RFC 2031 as the summary of the IETF-ISOC relationship. It is Informational, and the unit metadata lists nothing that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: How the Relationship Developed
sections.content:
The Internet Society (ISOC) provides a corporate home for the administrative entity that supports the IETF, the IAB and the IRTF. The IETF is primarily a volunteer organization that works by rough consensus and running code.

Legal, administrative and financial issues had long been an undesirable but unavoidable part of the IETF, so the Poised95 Working Group was set up in 1995. It concluded that ISOC, formed in 1992, was the best organization to handle these tasks. That led to documents such as RFC 2026 and RFC 2031. The IASA was defined in 2005 in RFC 4071 and RFC 4371.

In 2018 the IASA2 Working Group revised the structure as IASA 2.0. A key outcome was the IETF Administration Limited Liability Company (IETF LLC), formed as a subsidiary of ISOC.
sections.plainLanguage: A long time ago the IETF, a group of volunteer engineers, asked a helper organization to handle the paperwork and money. When the IETF reorganized in 2018, the arrangement needed to be written down again.

sections.title: Philosophy and Division of Responsibilities
sections.content:
ISOC and the IETF are described as philosophically aligned. ISOC advocates multistakeholder processes, and open standards are an explicit part of its mission.

The IETF remains responsible for the development and quality of Internet Standards. The RFC states that ISOC as an organization has no direct influence whatsoever on their technical content, although ISOC employees may contribute as individuals.
sections.plainLanguage: The IETF decides how the internet's rules work. Its helper is friendly and supportive but does not get a say in the technical details.

sections.title: Roles in Each Other's Work
sections.content:
ISOC plays a small role in the standards process. It appoints the IETF NomCom chair, confirms IAB candidates put forward by the NomCom, and acts as the last resort in the appeals process. It also keeps liaison relationships with other standards bodies, for example as a Sector Member of the ITU-T, and runs programs such as its IETF Policy Program. ISOC staff taking part in the IETF do so as individuals, not on institutional grounds.

The IETF in turn plays a role in governing ISOC: under ISOC's bylaws, the IETF appoints a set of trustees to the ISOC Board. The IAB charter makes the IAB a source of advice and guidance to ISOC's Board of Trustees and Officers on technical, architectural, procedural and policy matters.
sections.plainLanguage: The helper picks the person who runs the election committee and acts as a final referee in disputes. In return, the IETF chooses some of the helper's board members and gives it technical advice.

sections.title: The Legal Relationship
sections.content:
The IETF LLC is a disregarded limited liability company of ISOC, established to provide a corporate legal framework for activities of the IETF, IAB and IRTF. It was established by the ISOC / IETF LLC Agreement on August 27, 2018.

The IETF Trust provides legal protection for the RFC Series and other aspects of the IETF, including trademarks, copyrights and intellectual property rights. IETF standards documents can be freely downloaded, copied and distributed, although all rights to change them lie with the IETF. The creation of the IETF LLC changed how the Trust's trustees are selected but not the Trust's purpose or operation. One trustee is appointed by ISOC's Board of Trustees.
sections.plainLanguage: The IETF got its own legal box, owned by its helper, so it can sign contracts. A separate trust looks after the IETF's names and documents.

sections.title: Financial and Administrative Relationship
sections.content:
Under the Operating Agreement, ISOC has agreed to provide significant funding support for the IETF. The IETF LLC creates and manages the annual operating budget, negotiates and oversees contracts, fundraises, maintains bank accounts and carries liability insurance. It is run by a Board of Directors, one of whom is appointed by ISOC's Board of Trustees. The intention is that ISOC and the IETF LLC operate at arm's length.

The IETF LLC contracts with third parties for services, and some of those may be provided by ISOC or involve ISOC staff. Under IASA 2.0 the IETF LLC is solely responsible for its administration, including the IETF Trust, IAB, IESG, working groups and other IETF processes, as explored further in RFC 8711.
sections.plainLanguage: The helper gives the IETF a lot of money, but the IETF's own business arm decides how to spend it, hires the people, and keeps the books.
